name: Kings County
intro: Kings County is coextensive with the borough of Brooklyn, the most populous of New York City's five boroughs. It spans dense brownstone neighborhoods, industrial waterfront districts, and residential areas from Greenpoint to Coney Island. Most residents commute within the city by subway and bus.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Queens County
intro: Queens County is coextensive with the borough of Queens, the largest of the five boroughs by land area and the second most populous. It is among the most ethnically diverse counties in the United States, with major hubs in Flushing, Jamaica, and Long Island City. Residents commute by subway, bus, and the Long Island Rail Road.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: New York County
intro: New York County is coextensive with the borough of Manhattan, the commercial and cultural core of New York City. It is the destination for large daily commuter flows from the outer boroughs, Long Island, the Hudson Valley, and New Jersey. Housing stock is dominated by apartment buildings, from prewar walk-ups to high-rise towers.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Bronx County
intro: Bronx County is coextensive with the borough of the Bronx, the only NYC borough primarily on the U.S. mainland. It includes dense residential neighborhoods, Yankee Stadium, the Bronx Zoo, and large parks such as Van Cortlandt and Pelham Bay. Residents commute by subway, bus, and Metro-North.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Richmond County
intro: Richmond County is coextensive with the borough of Staten Island, the least populous of the five boroughs and the most suburban in character. It is connected to Brooklyn by the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and to Manhattan by the Staten Island Ferry. Single-family and townhouse housing dominates much of the borough.
permitNotes: Home-improvement contractors in New York City are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), and building permits are issued through the NYC Department of Buildings (DOB).

name: Nassau County
intro: Nassau County covers the western portion of Long Island immediately east of Queens, dominated by the large towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead, and Oyster Bay plus the cities of Glen Cove and Long Beach. It is a classic commuter county, with many residents riding the Long Island Rail Road into Manhattan. The county seat is Mineola.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-affairs office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments. Licensed trades such as electricians and plumbers are often licensed at the town or county level on Long Island.

name: Suffolk County
intro: Suffolk County occupies the central and eastern portion of Long Island, from the Nassau border out to Montauk and Orient Point. Its largest towns are Brookhaven, Islip, Babylon, Huntington, and Smithtown, and the county seat is Riverhead. Western Suffolk is heavily commuter-oriented via the Long Island Rail Road, while the East End is known for farms, vineyards, and beach communities.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-affairs office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments. Licensed trades such as electricians and plumbers are often licensed at the town or county level on Long Island.

name: Westchester County
intro: Westchester County lies immediately north of New York City in the lower Hudson Valley. Its largest municipalities are the cities of Yonkers, New Rochelle, Mount Vernon, and White Plains, the county seat, along with the large town of Greenburgh. Metro-North's Hudson, Harlem, and New Haven lines carry heavy commuter traffic into Grand Central Terminal.
permitNotes: Contractor licensing runs through the county consumer-protection office, while building permits are issued by individual town, city, and village building departments.

name: Rockland County
intro: Rockland County sits on the west bank of the Hudson River northwest of New York City, across the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge from Westchester. Its five towns are Ramapo, Clarkstown, Orangetown, Haverstraw, and Stony Point, with the county seat in New City. Commuters reach the city by bus, by NJ Transit rail lines, and via the bridge.
